questions.stem: Which of the following is a property of non-metals?

They are generally poor conductors of heat
questions.solution: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat, which is a characteristic property of this group. Metals, in contrast, are good conductors of heat and electricity. Lustrous and malleable properties are typically associated with metals, not non-metals.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of using a wooden handle on a metal spoon?
choices: To make it easier to hold
To prevent heat from transferring to the hand
questions.solution: Wood is a poor conductor of heat, so it prevents heat from transferring to the hand when using a metal spoon. The other options are incorrect because the primary function of the handle is not to make it easier to hold, lighter, or more durable, but to reduce heat transfer.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct observation from the experiment with iron nails in glass bottles?
choices: Iron nails show brown deposits in dry air only
Iron nails show brown deposits in water only
Iron nails show brown deposits in both dry air and water
Iron nails show brown deposits in the presence of both water and air
questions.solution: The experiment shows that brown deposits (rust) form only when both water and air are present. Bottle A (dry air) and B (water) do not show rust, but bottle C (both) does. Hence, the correct answer is that iron nails show brown deposits in the presence of both water and air. The other options are incorrect because they suggest rust forms in only one condition, which the experiment disproves.

questions.stem: What happens when magnesium ribbon is burned in air?
choices: It turns into a black powder
It turns into a white powder
questions.solution: When magnesium ribbon is burned in air, it reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide, which is a white powder. The flame produced during this reaction is bright white, not green or blue. Therefore, the correct answer is that it turns into a white powder.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances is stored in kerosene to prevent it from reacting with air and water?
questions.solution: Sodium is stored in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with oxygen and water in the air, which can lead to dangerous reactions. Kerosene prevents this by creating a barrier that isolates sodium from moisture and air. Copper, iron, and sulfur do not react as vigorously with air and water, so they do not require storage in kerosene.

hi.solution: सोडियम को केरोसीन में रखा जाता है क्योंकि यह हवा में ऑक्सीजन और पानी से तीव्र रूप से अभिक्रिया करता है, जो खतरनाक अभिक्रियाओं का कारण बन सकता है। केरोसीन इस अभिक्रिया को रोकता है क्योंकि यह नमी और हवा से सोडियम को अलग कर देता है। तांबा, लोहा और सल्फर हवा और पानी के साथ इतना तीव्र रूप से अभिक्रिया नहीं करते हैं, इसलिए इन्हें केरोसीन में नहीं रखा जाता है।

questions.stem: Which of the following properties is shown by a piece of iron when it is dropped on the floor?
questions.solution: Metals like iron are sonorous, which means they produce a ringing sound when dropped on the floor. This property is called sonority. The other options are incorrect because non-metals like coal and wood produce dull sounds, and metals are not brittle or soft.

questions.stem: A metal that is used in making food packaging materials is chosen because it is cheap and can be easily shaped. Which metal is this?
questions.solution: Aluminium is the correct answer because it is lightweight, inexpensive, and highly malleable, making it ideal for shaping into food packaging. Copper is more expensive and less malleable, iron is prone to rusting, and gold is too costly and not suitable for packaging materials.
